title: Temporal Cohort Holdback Adapter for continuous batcher (cohort-aware wait-offsets, starvation prevention)
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: We observed recurring tail-latency spikes during mixed-weight workloads where a small cohort of KV-heavy requests would repeatedly preempt continuous batch windows and cause starvation for short low-cost requests. Previous mitigations (grace windows, soft reservations) reduced p99 but caused throughput regressions under bursty traffic.

Proposal: Introduce a Temporal Cohort Holdback Adapter in the continuous batching admission path. The adapter maintains short-lived cohort tokens derived from recent request fingerprints (kernel type, KV hint presence, sequence length bucket). For cohorts that have consumed >X% of batch slots over a rolling window, the adapter introduces an exponentially decaying wait-offset that delays new arrivals from that cohort by a small jittered amount. The goal is to: (1) prevent cohort monopolization without hard preemption, (2) preserve KV cache locality by keeping warm cohorts but preventing tail monopolies, (3) provide a smooth, measurable knob (holdback decay, threshold, jitter) for SRE to tune.

Design notes: 1) Admission path changes live in runtime/batcher/admission_adapter.{cpp,h}. The adapter hooks into the existing slot allocator and exposes cohort metadata to the scheduler as lightweight tags. 2) Cohorts are computed from a 3-tuple: model_family, kv_hint_present (bool), and quantized input length bucket. 3) Holdback tokens are implemented as a fixed-size LRU ring per worker to cap memory and avoid global coordination. 4) Decay is time-based (half-life default 1.2s) and multiplicative; jitter is applied to avoid synchronized waves. 5) The adapter only biases admission time (wait-offset) — it does not change kernel selection or KV pinning logic. Where beneficial we emit scheduler hints so kernel selection can prefer paths that are less KV-heavy for temporarily delayed cohorts.

Safety and rollout: Feature guarded behind runtime flag `enable_temporal_cohort_holdback`. Default disabled in main; enabled in canary. Configurable params surfaced in console (holdback_threshold_pct, half_life_ms, jitter_ms, max_offset_ms). We included a canary rollout plan: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 72 hours with automated p99 and throughput checks.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for the ring buffer and decay semantics; integration tests in batcher test harness simulating heterogeneous cohorts; end-to-end perf harness measuring tail latencies with realistic KV-heavy traces. We also added a regression test for KV cache hit-rate to ensure no meaningful degradation.

Benchmarks: See summary below. Observability: New metrics (cohort_id, holdback_offset_ms, cohort_consumption_pct) emitted as tags in the per-route metrics; dashboards updated under Observability->Batcher Cohorts.

Follow-ups: (a) investigate adaptive kernel fallbacks when cohort holdbacks approach max_offset to reduce cost impact, (b) add a control-plane endpoint to inject synthetic cohorts for canary stress tests, (c) consider cross-worker cohort telemetry for multi-worker correlated bursts.
commits: 3 commits: (1) initial adapter implementation + tests; (2) race fix in ring buffer and reduced memory footprint; (3) perf tuning and metrics + docs
review_comments: Owen Chen: Nice approach. Two asks: (1) please add a small e2e that replays the kv-heavy trace and asserts p99 < baseline+10ms, (2) document the knobs exposed to customers in the console UI.
Maya Patel: Added the e2e harness and console fields; pushed a follow-up commit. Also added the holdback metrics to the dashboards.
Ravi Kumar: Found a potential ABA race in the ring LRU when concurrent inserts collide; suggested using a versioned compare-and-swap. I pushed a patch recommending a lightweight sequence guard.
Maya Patel: Addressed ABA race by moving to sequence-guarded CAS and added unit tests that reproduce the race under stress. Re-ran CI.
Elena Sokolov: Perf numbers look good; please ensure the default decay is conservative (we use 1.2s in this PR). Approving pending CI pass.
CI Bot: All checks passed on run #3. Merging to main with squash.
benchmark_results: Baseline (no holdback): p50=18ms p95=64ms p99=182ms throughput=1250 req/s
Canary (holdback default): p50=19ms p95=58ms p99=124ms throughput=1210 req/s (-3.2%)
KV-heavy burst (stress): p50=24ms p95=110ms p99=220ms baseline; with holdback p50=25ms p95=78ms p99=128ms (major p99 improvement)
KV cache hit-rate: baseline 87.3% vs holdback 86.9% (within noise)
release_notes: Add temporal cohort holdback adapter to continuous batcher to reduce cohort monopolization and p99 latency spikes under mixed workloads.
Default disabled; configurable in Console and via runtime flag. See docs/perf/continuous-batcher-cohorts.md for tuning guidance.
No breaking changes to public API. Small throughput regressions possible when enabled (default conservative params).
merge_outcome: Merged to main via squash; feature gate off by default. Canary rollout started after merge: 1% traffic, automated p99/throughput checks configured.
notes_for_oncall: If canary p99 regresses >20% from baseline, disable `enable_temporal_cohort_holdback` and roll back canary; check cohort metrics for a mis-tuned threshold that can be reduced quickly.
